steps.title: Open the Structure page
steps.narration: Let's open the Structure page, where real stock price history and its support-and-resistance levels come together in one view.
steps.point_out: The 'Fetch from Yahoo Finance' panel at the top, and a second 'Load' form just below it.

expect.text: Choose a symbol and an as-of time, then Load, to see its S/R levels and confluence zones.

steps.title: Type in a stock symbol
steps.narration: Type a stock symbol into the fetch panel — we'll use AAPL.
steps.point_out: The Symbol field now reads AAPL.

steps.title: Pick a daily timeframe
steps.narration: Choose the daily timeframe, so each candle represents one trading day.

steps.title: Set the start of the date range
steps.narration: Enter the start of the window of history to fetch, in UTC.
steps.point_out: The Start field is filled in.

steps.title: Set the end of the date range
steps.narration: And the end of that window.
steps.point_out: The End field is filled in, and the Fetch button is no longer greyed out.

steps.title: Fetch real bars from Yahoo Finance
steps.narration: Click once and the app pulls real historical prices straight from Yahoo Finance — no signup, no fee — and draws the chart immediately.
steps.point_out: A real candlestick chart appears with dashed support-and-resistance lines, and a 'Confluence zones' list below shows Class A/B/C zones with scores.

expect.text: Level lines span every recorded timeframe.

steps.title: See exactly where the data came from
steps.narration: A small badge above the chart names the real source of this data, so where the numbers came from is never a mystery.
steps.point_out: A dark chip reading 'feed' next to 'Yahoo Finance' in bold sits cleanly above the chart, fully readable with nothing overlapping it.

steps.title: Ask about a symbol with no saved history
steps.narration: Now let's try a symbol that has never been fetched before — TSLA — using the separate Load form below.
steps.point_out: The Symbol field in the Load form now reads TSLA.

steps.title: Set the as-of time
steps.narration: Enter a time to check its levels as of.
steps.point_out: The As-of field is filled in.

steps.title: An honest message when there's no data yet
steps.narration: Instead of a blank or broken-looking chart, the app plainly tells you there's nothing recorded for this symbol yet.
steps.point_out: The message 'No bar series recorded for TSLA.' appears, with 'Recording historical bars needs provider credentials.' underneath — no chart, no badge, no zones.

expect.text: No bar series recorded for TSLA.

steps.title: Switch back to a symbol with real data
steps.narration: Switch the symbol back to AAPL, which does have saved history.
steps.point_out: The Symbol field now reads AAPL again.

steps.title: The original Load button still works
steps.narration: The original Load button — the one that predates today's fetch feature — still pulls up a real chart exactly as it always has.
steps.point_out: The candlestick chart and confluence zones reappear for AAPL.

expect.text: Level lines span every recorded timeframe.

steps.title: Try an invalid date range
steps.narration: Let's see what happens if the dates are entered backwards — end before start.
steps.point_out: The Start field in the fetch panel now holds the later date.

steps.title: Finish the backwards range
steps.narration: And the End field now holds the earlier date.
steps.point_out: The End field now holds a date before the Start field's date.

steps.title: Nothing is ever faked
steps.narration: The app refuses to guess — it shows a clear, honest error instead of ever making up data.
steps.point_out: An amber panel reads 'end must be after start,' followed by 'Nothing cached and nothing fabricated is shown in its place.' The chart above stays exactly as it was.
